title: Why studying females reveals more about aging: The reproductive resilience hypothesis for the evolution of sex-specific aging.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC flags show no open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no data links, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links (GEO, SRA, BioProject), no Zenodo/Dryad hits on the DOI.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: a perspective/hypothesis article proposing the 'reproductive resilience hypothesis' (RRH) for sex differences in aging; it describes no new dataset.

a1_downloadable.note: Conceptual perspective paper with no deposited data; no supplement, accessions or repository records found (checked via Europe PMC, NCBI links and Zenodo/Dryad search).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No dataset exists, so there is no label column; any label (e.g. sex-specific lifespan) would have to be assembled from other sources.

honest_claim_h3: None: the paper is a hypothesis piece with no data to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use species life-history traits (age at maturity, caregiving length) to predict how much longer females live than males.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need species-level life-history and sex-specific lifespan records from outside databases; this paper supplies none; count unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Female-minus-male lifespan gap per species, which would come from external zoo or wild-population records, not this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would test the paper's hypothesis quantitatively, but it is a different project built on other datasets, not this paper.

label_elsewhere.why: Reject; no data in this paper.

ml_idea: None from this paper. A separate project could test the RRH (reproductive resilience hypothesis) on external comparative lifespan databases, but that is unrelated to this paper's data.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: Europe PMC and repository search show no data attached.

verdict_reason: Conceptual perspective article proposing an evolutionary hypothesis; it has no dataset, supplement or accessions, so Part A1 fails.
